These effects are caused by digitalis inhibiting:

answers.option: Na+/K+ ATPase of the myocyte membrane

question: Compensatory increases in heart rate and renin release that occur in heart failure may be alleviated by which of the following drugs?

A 57-year-old man with a history of atrial fibrillation is diagnosed with classic angina. Which of the following would be contraindicated in this patient?

A 64-year-old man with a history of systolic HF develops pulmonary edema with difficulty breathing. Which drug is the best choice to acutely increase cardiac output in this patient within the next 30 mins?

A 10-year-old boy with a known history of a ventricular septal defect presents with 7 days of fever, malaise, and decreased appetite. On examination, his temperature is 38.7°C, and he has a new systolic murmur at the left lower sternal border. You note splinter hemorrhages on his fingernails and tender nodules on the pads of his fingers. Blood cultures are pending. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to support the diagnosis of infective endocarditis in this patient?

answers.option: Perform transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) to look for vegetations
Order a chest X-ray to evaluate for septic emboli
Schedule an MRI brain to evaluate for silent embolic strokes
Start empirical intravenous antibiotics immediately without further testing
Repeat blood cultures only after the patient becomes afebrile

question: A 7-year-old girl with no known cardiac history is admitted with a 10-day history of intermittent fever and lethargy. Blood cultures grow Streptococcus viridans in 3 separate samples. Transthoracic echocardiography reveals a 6 mm vegetation on the mitral valve. She is hemodynamically stable and has no signs of heart failure or embolic events. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management step?

answers.option: Discharge with follow-up if fever settles within 48 hours
Start empirical oral antibiotics and monitor response
Refer for urgent surgical removal of the vegetation
Begin anticoagulation to prevent embolic complications
Start intravenous antibiotic based on sensitivity and monitor

question: A 9-year-old previously healthy boy presents with a 6-day history of high-grade fever and fatigue. He has no known congenital heart disease or prior medical issues. On examination, he is febrile (39.2°C) with a new pansystolic murmur at the apex. His skin shows multiple excoriated, crusted lesions on the arms and legs, consistent with superinfected eczema. Blood cultures grow Staphylococcus aureus. Echocardiography reveals a mobile vegetation on the anterior mitral leaflet. Which of the following is the most likely source of the infective organism in this case of native valve endocarditis?

answers.option: Undiagnosed bicuspid aortic valve from birth
Poorly controlled eczema with secondary bacterial infection
Recent travel to a region endemic for rheumatic fever
Central venous catheter use during infancy

question: A 65-year-old male was brought to the emergency department and reported to have complained of right-sided hemiparesis, his blood pressure was recorded, and it was 170/110 mmHg, and repeated twice. He was labeled as hypertensive. In which stage of hypertension is this classified?
Which one of the following is the non-modifiable risk factor for developing cardiovascular diseases?
Which one of the following is the most appropriate preventive strategy to control myocardial infarction?

A 55-year-old male with a family history of hypertension is concerned about his risk. He has a BMI of 29, consumes a diet high in processed foods, and reports a sedentary lifestyle. His blood pressure is consistently in the high-normal range (135/85 mmHg). Which of the following modifications can the patient implement to prevent the onset of hypertension?

A 48-year-old female presents for a routine check-up. She is obese (BMI 32), has a waist circumference of 95 cm, and her fasting blood glucose is 115 mg/dL. Her blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, and her triglyceride levels are elevated. She has no personal history of cardiovascular disease but her father had a myocardial infarction at age 55. Which of the following conditions is most likely present and represents a significant cardiovascular risk factor?

A 64-year-old man presents to the emergency department with 45 minutes of substernal chest pain radiating to his left arm. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia. His ECG shows 1.5 mm ST depression in leads V4-V6 and T-wave inversions in leads II, III, and aVF. Troponin I is mildly elevated. He is hemodynamically stable. He receives aspirin, clopidogrel, a statin, and a beta-blocker. After 6 hours of observation and medical therapy, his pain persists, and repeated ECGs show deepening ST depressions in the same leads. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

answers.option: Immediate coronary angiography with intent for PCI
Perform stress echocardiography to guide further treatment
Add intravenous heparin and discharge if pain resolves
Continue medical management and monitor troponins

question: A 38-year-old woman presents with acute-onset chest pain and shortness of breath. Her ECG is unremarkable, but high-sensitivity troponin is elevated and rising. Coronary angiography reveals no significant coronary artery obstruction. Cardiac MRI confirms apical ballooning of the left ventricle. Which of the following mechanisms most accurately explains the pathogenesis of this patient's presentation?

answers.option: Coronary vasospasm leading to transient ischemia
Demand ischemia due to uncontrolled hypertension
Microvascular obstruction due to cholesterol emboli
Plaque rupture with superimposed thrombus formation

question: A 22-year-old female athlete collapses during a track event. She is resuscitated and brought to the emergency department. Physical exam reveals a systolic murmur that increases with Valsalva. Her ECG shows deep Q waves in the lateral leads and LVH. Echocardiogram reveals asymmetric septal hypertrophy with systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve and an LV outflow gradient of 75 mmHg. Which of the following interventions is contraindicated in this patient?

A 70-year-old man presents with exertional chest pain and occasional dizziness. On examination, you detect a harsh systolic ejection murmur best heard in the right second intercostal space, radiating to the carotids. His pulse is slow-rising and low volume, and there is a narrow pulse pressure. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old woman presents with increasing breathlessness. On examination, she has a pansystolic murmur loudest at the apical area. There is radiation of the murmur to the axilla. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the murmur in this patient?
During a cardiovascular examination, a medical student notes a displaced apex beat in the 6th intercostal space, mid-clavicular line. What does a displaced apex beat usually indicate?

He has no risk factors for IHD. Immediately, an ECG was done, which shows diffuse ST elevations in precordial and limb leads. What is the most likely diagnosis?

He has no risk factors for IHD. Immediately, an ECG is done, which shows diffuse ST elevations in precordial and limb leads. What is the treatment of choice in this clinical condition?

A 68-year-old man presents to the emergency department with crushing substernal chest pain, tachycardia, diaphoresis, nausea, vomiting, and dyspnea. ECG shows ST elevation. What is the most appropriate medication to relieve this pain?

He also complained of jaw pain and, on palpation, had prominent temporal arteries. Biopsy of the temporal arteries showed granulomatous inflammation. What is the best possible diagnosis?

A 15-year-old girl presents with syncope; she had been complaining of dyspnea and chest pain for a month. Vital signs were stable with a blood pressure of 120/70 mmHg, pulse rate of 135 bpm, respiratory rate of 16 breaths per minute, and temperature of 36.7 °C. On physical exam, pupils were equal, reactive to light, chest was clear. Cardiovascular exam was notable for a systolic murmur at the apex and irregularly irregular rhythm. The abdomen was unremarkable. ECG showed atrial fibrillation, and echocardiography showed mitral regurgitation and a large mass in the atrium. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old male is found with a deep incised wound on the neck extending from one angle of the mandible to the other. The wound has sharp, well-defined margins and no surrounding bruising. Which of the following features most strongly suggests that this is a homicidal cut-throat wound rather than suicidal?

answers.option: Presence of blood in the trachea
Absence of hesitation cuts around the wound
Wound directed from left to right and slightly downwards
Wound located above the thyroid cartilage

question: A 35-year-old woman is found dead with multiple stab wounds over the chest and abdomen. On autopsy, several wounds have different directions and depths. Which feature is most helpful in differentiating homicidal stab wounds from suicidal stab wounds?

answers.option: Stab wound located over precordial area
Presence of defensive wounds on forearms and hands
Small, superficial puncture wounds adjacent to main wound
Single stab wound with vertical direction
Absence of hilt mark around the wound

question: During autopsy, a body shows a long, deep incised wound parallel to the wrist crease, along with several other superficial cuts on the forearm. What is the most likely interpretation of this finding?

answers.option: Accidental injury while handling a sharp object

question: A 40-year-old man is brought dead after an assault. On examination, there is a lacerated wound on the scalp with abraded and bruised margins. The underlying bone shows a depressed fracture. Which of the following best explains why the wound appears incised despite being caused by a blunt weapon?

answers.option: Presence of a sharp edge on the weapon
Scalp lacerations always mimic incised wounds
Crushing of skin and subcutaneous tissues against underlying bone
Stretching of skin fibers along lines of cleavage

question: A farmer is found with multiple contusions and abrasions on the back and extremities after a fall from height. Some abrasions are scabbed while others are reddish. Which feature best helps in estimating the age of abrasions in this case?

answers.option: Color of the scab and surrounding tissue changes
